entry: American film and television actor. He attracted wider attention with *Platoon* (1986) and *Wall Street* (1987). He starred as Charlie Harper on the [[CBS]] sitcom *Two and a Half Men* (2003–2011), earning US$1.8 million per episode in 2010, when he was the highest-paid actor on television. He was terminated from the series in March 2011 after public substance-abuse problems and comments about its creator, [[Chuck Lorre]]. In 2015 he publicly disclosed that he was [[HIV]] positive. In 2025 he was the subject of the [[Netflix]] documentary *Aka Charlie Sheen*.

South African-born American actress and producer. She won an Academy Award for Best Actress for playing serial killer [[Aileen Wuornos]] in *Monster* (2003), becoming the first South African to win an acting Oscar. Her other films include *The Devil's Advocate* (1997), *Mad Max: Fury Road* (2015) and *Atomic Blonde* (2017). Since the early 2000s she has produced films through her company Denver and Delilah Productions. She became an American citizen in 2007 while retaining South African citizenship.

English novelist and poet. She is best known for *[[Jane Eyre]]*, published in 1847 under the pseudonym Currer Bell and since acknowledged as a classic of English literature. Her first novel, *The Professor*, was rejected by publishers. While a teacher at a school in [[Brussels]], she fell in love with its director, Constantin Heger, who inspired the character Rochester in *Jane Eyre*. She married Arthur Bell Nicholls, her father's curate, in 1854, and died while pregnant, possibly of [[Tuberculosis|tuberculosis]] or hyperemesis gravidarum.

Most populous city in [[North Carolina]] (pop., 2020: 874,579). Named for Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, queen consort of Great Britain and Ireland from 1761, it was incorporated in 1768. Railroads made it a regional trading hub after the [[American Civil War]], and by 1910 it had surpassed Wilmington as the state's largest city. It is the headquarters of [[Bank of America]] and, with other Charlotte-based financial institutions, the second-largest banking center in the nation. The city is home to the [[NASCAR]] Hall of Fame and the Carolina Panthers of the NFL.

English actress. She began as a model and appeared in *Georgy Girl* (1966) before making French and Italian arthouse films, including Luchino Visconti's *The Damned* (1969) and Liliana Cavani's *The Night Porter* (1974). In the 2000s she became the muse of French director François Ozon. For *45 Years* (2015) she won the Berlin Film Festival Award and the European Film Award for Best Actress, and she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress. She played Dr. Evelyn Vogel in *[[Dexter (TV series)|Dexter]]* (2013).

American actor and political activist. He won an Academy Award for Best Actor for the title role in *[[Ben-Hur (1959 film)|Ben-Hur]]* (1959). He also starred as [[Moses]] in *The Ten Commandments* (1956) and in science-fiction films such as *Planet of the Apes* (1968). In the 1950s and early 1960s he openly denounced racism and supported the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]]. In 1987 he left the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] to become a Republican, supporting [[Ronald Reagan]]. He was president of the National Rifle Association from 1998 to 2003, and in 2002 he announced that he had [[Alzheimer's disease]].

Largest of the five known natural satellites of the dwarf planet [[Pluto]]. Charon has a mean radius of 606 km (377 mi) and half the diameter of Pluto. It was discovered in 1978 at the United States Naval Observatory in Washington, D.C., using photographic plates. The two bodies are [[Tidal locking|tidally locked]], so the barycenter of the system lies outside Pluto. Its reddish-brown north polar cap is composed of tholins, organic macromolecules. The [[New Horizons]] spacecraft approached Charon to within 27,000 km (17,000 mi) in 2015.

Paraphyletic group of freshwater [[Green algae|green algae]]. Land plants (Embryophyta) emerged deep within Charophyta, possibly from terrestrial unicellular forms, with the class Zygnematophyceae as their sister group. The charophytes' sister group is [[Chlorophyta]]. Zygnematophyceae reproduce sexually by conjugation, in which the contents of two cells fuse. Stoneworts (Charales) and Coleochaetales have flagellate sperm and are the parenchymatous orders that are the closest relatives of land plants. Charophyta is now treated as a synonym of Streptophyta. Its name comes from the genus *Chara*. Fossil stoneworts of early [[Devonian|Devonian]] age have been described from the Rhynie chert of Scotland, and stoneworts are freshwater and brackish algae with slender stems.

Color between [[Yellow]] and green, also called yellow-green. It was named for its resemblance to the French liqueur green chartreuse, introduced in 1764. Its wavelength is near 547.5 nm. Chartreuse yellow, a yellow mixed with a small amount of green, is used on traffic safety vests for visibility. From the 2000s the shade became popular in office decor and other products, helped by the success of the *Shrek* franchise.

[[Generative AI]] chatbot developed by OpenAI. Released on November 30, 2022, it uses [[Large language model|large language models]] to generate text, speech and images in response to user prompts. It reached 100 million monthly active users two months after release. Plugins added in March 2023 included web browsing and code interpretation, and ChatGPT Search later allowed it to search the web. Critics cite its [[Hallucination|hallucinations]], biases, potential for academic dishonesty, and the use of copyrighted content as training data.

Software application, or associated user interface, designed to converse through text or speech. Originally called chatterbot, chatbots date to the 1960s. Joseph Weizenbaum's ELIZA, published in 1966, produced an illusion of understanding by recognizing clue words and returning prepared responses. The [[Turing test]], proposed by [[Alan Turing]] in 1950, is a criterion of intelligence based on a program's ability to impersonate a human in conversation. Chatbots based on deep learning became popular during the [[AI boom]] of the 2020s, with generative chatbots such as [[ChatGPT]], Gemini, DeepSeek and Grok. Customer service is a major use.

Pre-Columbian Andean civilization of highland [[Peru]]. It was the main culture of the Early Horizon period in highland Peru, and its influence extended to other civilizations along the Peruvian coast. Its best-known site, Chavín de Huántar, is a UNESCO [[World Heritage Site]]. The temple there had canals that drained rainy-season water, which rushing through them produced a roaring sound that emulates a jaguar, a sacred animal. The temple was built of white granite and black limestone, neither found near the site, so workers brought them from far away. The culture was skilled in metallurgy and soldering, domesticated [[Llama|llamas]], and cultivated [[Potato|potatoes]], [[Quinoa]] and [[Maize]]. Its language is unknown, and some anthropologists have proposed a form of Proto-Quechuan.

Argentine Marxist revolutionary and guerrilla leader. He was a major figure of the [[Cuban Revolution]], promoted to second-in-command of the insurgents and playing a pivotal role in the two-year guerrilla campaign that deposed the Batista regime. In the new government he served as minister of industries and president of the National Bank, and he helped spearhead a literacy campaign. His role in bringing Soviet nuclear-armed missiles to Cuba precipitated the [[Cuban Missile Crisis]]. He left Cuba in 1965 to foment revolution in Africa and South America, and in [[Bolivia]] he was captured by Bolivian forces, assisted by the CIA, and executed. Supporters regard him as a symbol of anti-imperialism; critics accuse him of promoting authoritarianism and endorsing violence against opponents. *Time* named him one of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century.

Republic of [[Russia]] in the [[Caucasus|North Caucasus]] (pop., 2021: over 1.5 million). It covers 16,500 sq km, and its capital and largest city is Grozny. Most residents are Chechens, part of the Nakh peoples, who adhere primarily to Islam. After the [[Soviet Union]] dissolved in 1991, the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria declared independence. The [[First Chechen War]] (1994–1996) left it with de facto independence, although it remained part of Russia. Russian federal control was restored in the [[Second Chechen War]] (1999–2009). Politics was later dominated by Akhmad Kadyrov, a former mufti, and then by his son Ramzan Kadyrov. Supporters credit the Kadyrov administration with reconstruction and a decline in separatist violence; critics cite authoritarian practices and curtailed civil liberties.

Group of strategy [[Board game|board games]] for two players, also called draughts. Players move uniform pieces diagonally forward and capture opposing pieces by jumping over them, which is mandatory in most official rules. The most popular forms in English-speaking countries are American checkers, played on an 8×8 board, and international draughts, played on a 10×10 board. Canadian checkers and the [[Malaysia|Malaysian]] and [[Singapore|Singaporean]] variants are played on a 12×12 board. A piece that reaches the far row becomes a king, which can move backward. In 2007 a team of Canadian computer scientists led by Jonathan Schaeffer weakly solved American checkers; from the standard starting position, perfect play results in a draw.

American television [[Sitcom|sitcom]] set in a Boston bar. Created by Glen Charles, Les Charles and James Burrows, it aired on [[NBC]] for eleven seasons from 1982 to 1993. Its central character is Sam Malone, a former relief pitcher for the [[Boston Red Sox]] who owns the bar. After nearly being canceled in its first season, it became a ratings success and won 28 Primetime Emmy Awards from 117 nominations. Its finale was the most-watched single TV episode of the 1990s, and the show was followed by the spin-off *[[Frasier]]* (1993–2004).

Large [[Felidae|feline]] of the genus *Acinonyx*. The cheetah (*Acinonyx jubatus*) is the fastest land animal, capable of running 93–104 km/h (58–65 mph) in short bursts. It has a tawny coat marked with solid black spots and weighs 21–65 kg. Cheetahs stalk prey within 30–200 m before a high-speed charge, killing with a throat bite. Females raise cubs while living a nomadic life, and males form coalitions or solitary territories. Cubs are highly vulnerable to [[Lion|lions]] and [[Hyena|hyenas]]. Four subspecies are recognized, native to [[Africa]] and central Iran. The global population was estimated at 6,517 mature individuals in 2021, and the species is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List. Cheetahs were tamed in ancient [[Ancient Egypt|Egypt]] and have been kept in zoos since the early 19th century.

Subphylum of [[Arthropod|arthropods]] that includes horseshoe crabs, sea spiders and arachnids. The name comes from the chelicerae, the only appendages that appear before the mouth. In most groups these are pincers for feeding, but in [[Spider|spiders]] they form fangs that inject venom. Chelicerates have segmented bodies covered in a cuticle of [[Chitin|chitin]] and proteins. Marine species breathe through gills, while air-breathing forms have book lungs and tracheae. Chelicerates split from the Mandibulata by the [[Cambrian|mid-Cambrian]]. Over 77,000 well-identified air-breathing species are known. Venom evolved three times, in spiders, scorpions and pseudoscorpions. [[Mite|Mites]] transmit diseases to humans and their [[Livestock]], and the blood of [[Horseshoe crab|horseshoe crabs]] is used to test for contaminant bacteria.

American activist and whistleblower; former Army intelligence analyst. In 2010 she disclosed nearly 750,000 classified or sensitive military and diplomatic documents to [[WikiLeaks]], concerning operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. In 2013 a court-martial convicted her of Espionage Act violations and other offenses but acquitted her of aiding the enemy, and she was sentenced to 35 years. President [[Barack Obama]] commuted the sentence in 2017. In 2013 she stated that she had had a female gender identity since childhood. In 2019 and 2020 she was jailed for contempt for refusing to testify before a grand jury investigating [[Julian Assange]].

Administrative center and largest city of Chelyabinsk Oblast, [[Russia]]. It is Russia's seventh-largest city, with over 1.1 million people, and the second-largest in the Ural Federal District after [[Yekaterinburg]]. It lies east of the southern [[Ural Mountains]] along the Miass River. The fortress of Chelyaba was founded there in 1736 on the site of a Bashkir village. Railway links, including the [[Trans-Siberian Railway]], spurred growth in the early 20th century. Under the [[Soviet Union]] it became a major industrial center, and during [[World War II]] it was a major contributor to tank and ammunition manufacture. In 2013 an asteroid exploded in the atmosphere over the city, injuring roughly 1,500 residents, mostly from flying glass.

Scientific discipline between [[Chemistry|chemistry]] and [[Biology|biology]]. It applies chemical techniques, and often small molecules made by synthetic chemistry, to study and manipulate biological systems. Although often confused with [[Biochemistry]], which studies the chemistry of biomolecules, chemical biology focuses on using chemical tools to address biological questions. In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler synthesized urea from inorganic starting materials, an early example of synthetic chemistry advancing biology that weakened the notion of vitalism. Glycobiology, the study of [[Carbohydrate|carbohydrates]], uses synthetic sugars to probe cell function. Combinatorial chemistry synthesizes large numbers of related compounds for high-throughput screening, and chemical synthesis of [[Protein|proteins]] allows the introduction of non-natural amino acids.

Engineering discipline concerned with the design and operation of [[Chemical plant|chemical plants]]. Chemical engineers develop economical processes to convert raw materials into useful products, drawing on chemistry, physics, mathematics, biology and economics. Their work ranges from [[Nanotechnology|nanomaterials]] in the laboratory to large-scale industrial processes, including safety and hazard assessments, process design and control. The term is credited to the English consultant George E. Davis, and its use dates to about 1890. Advances in biochemical engineering in the 1940s allowed mass production of antibiotics such as [[Penicillin]] and streptomycin. Safety concerns followed the 1974 Flixborough disaster in the United Kingdom, which resulted in 28 deaths, and the [[Bhopal disaster]] in India, which resulted in at least 4,000 deaths.

Symbolic representation of a [[Chemical reaction|chemical reaction]] using [[Chemical formula|formulas]] and symbols. Reactants are listed on the left and products on the right, separated by an arrow that shows the direction of the reaction. Coefficients give the number of entities of each substance, and a coefficient of 1 is left unwritten. For example, [[Hydrochloric acid|hydrochloric acid]] reacting with [[Sodium|sodium]] is written 2HCl + 2Na → 2NaCl + H₂. Physical states may be added in parentheses: (s) for solid, (l) for liquid, (g) for gas and (aq) for aqueous solution. Symbols above the arrow can denote heat (Δ), light (hν) or a [[Catalysis|catalyst]]. The first chemical equation was diagrammed by Jean Beguin in 1615.

State of a [[Chemical reaction|chemical reaction]] in which reactants and products have concentrations that no longer change with time. It results when the forward reaction proceeds at the same rate as the reverse reaction, a condition known as dynamic equilibrium. Molecules keep reacting even though net concentrations stay constant. The concept was developed in 1803, after Berthollet found that some reactions are reversible. In 1865 Guldberg and Waage proposed the law of mass action, which defines an equilibrium constant that depends on [[Temperature|temperature]], though the law applies only to single-step reactions. Le Châtelier's principle (1884) predicts that a disturbed equilibrium shifts to partly reverse the change. A catalyst speeds both reactions equally, so it does not change the equilibrium constant.

Notation for the composition and structure of chemical compounds. Formulas use element symbols with subscripts for atom counts. An empirical formula gives the simplest ratio of elements, such as C₂H₅ for [[Butane]], while a molecular formula gives the exact count, C₄H₁₀. Structural formulas show bonding patterns; a condensed formula such as CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ is written as a line of text. Ionic compounds may be written as (NH₄)₂SO₄ for [[Ammonium sulfate]]. Formulas also describe chemical groups, classes of compounds such as amines, and polymers such as [[Polyethylene]]. Unlike text notations such as SMILES and InChI, formulas are intended to be read by people.
